Function.IsFixedPt.code: Function.IsFixedPt.{u} {α : Type u} (f : α → α) (x : α) : Prop
Function.IsFixedPt.comment: A point `x` is a fixed point of `f : α → α` if `f x = x`.
Function.IsFixedPt.fullDefinition: def IsFixedPt (f : α → α) (x : α) :=   f x = x
Function.IsFixedPt.description: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.

Function.isFixedPt_id.code: Function.isFixedPt_id.{u} {α : Type u} (x : α) : IsFixedPt id x
Function.isFixedPt_id.comment: Every point is a fixed point of `id`.

explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.

Function.isFixedPt_id.description: Every point is a fixed point of the identity function.

Function.IsFixedPt.eq.code: Function.IsFixedPt.eq.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : IsFixedPt f x) : f x = x
Function.IsFixedPt.eq.comment: If `x` is a fixed point of `f`, then `f x = x`. This is useful, e.g., for `rw` or `simp`.

explanatories.Function.Semiconj.eq: There is no specific concept or result to summarize, as no definition or theorem is provided.

Function.IsFixedPt.eq.description: If a point is a fixed point of a function, then applying the function to that point yields the point itself.

Function.IsFixedPt.comp.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.comp.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : α → α} {x : α} (hf : IsFixedPt f x) (hg : IsFixedPt g x) :
  IsFixedPt (f ∘ g) x
Function.IsFixedPt.comp.comment: If `x` is a fixed point of `f` and `g`, then it is a fixed point of `f ∘ g`.
Function.IsFixedPt.comp.description: If a point is a fixed point of two functions, then it is also a fixed point of their composition.

Function.IsFixedPt.iterate.code: Function.IsFixedPt.iterate.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : IsFixedPt f x) (n : ℕ) : IsFixedPt f^[n] x
Function.IsFixedPt.iterate.comment: If `x` is a fixed point of `f`, then it is a fixed point of `f^[n]`.
Function.IsFixedPt.iterate.description: If a point is a fixed point of a function, then it is also a fixed point of the function applied repeatedly any number of times.

Function.IsFixedPt.left_of_comp.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.left_of_comp.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : α → α} {x : α} (hfg : IsFixedPt (f ∘ g) x)
  (hg : IsFixedPt g x) : IsFixedPt f x
Function.IsFixedPt.left_of_comp.comment: If `x` is a fixed point of `f ∘ g` and `g`, then it is a fixed point of `f`.
Function.IsFixedPt.left_of_comp.description: If a point is a fixed point of a composition of two functions and the second function, then it is also a fixed point of the first function.

Function.IsFixedPt.to_leftInverse.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.to_leftInverse.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : α → α} {x : α} (hf : IsFixedPt f x) (h : LeftInverse g f) :
  IsFixedPt g x
Function.IsFixedPt.to_leftInverse.comment:
If `x` is a fixed point of `f` and `g` is a left inverse of `f`, then `x` is a fixed
point of `g`.

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.

Function.IsFixedPt.to_leftInverse.description: If a point is a fixed point of a function and another function serves as a left inverse to it, then that point is also a fixed point of the left inverse function.

Function.IsFixedPt.map.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.map.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {fa : α → α} {fb : β → β} {x : α} (hx : IsFixedPt fa x)
  {g : α → β} (h : Semiconj g fa fb) : IsFixedPt fb (g x)
Function.IsFixedPt.map.comment:
If `g` (semi)conjugates `fa` to `fb`, then it sends fixed points of `fa` to fixed points
of `fb`.

explanatories.Function.Semiconj: A function is said to semiconjugate two mappings if applying the function before one mapping is the same as applying the other mapping after the function.

Function.IsFixedPt.map.description: If one function semi-conjugates another, then it maps fixed points of the first function to fixed points of the second function.

Function.IsFixedPt.apply.code: Function.IsFixedPt.apply.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} {x : α} (hx : IsFixedPt f x) : IsFixedPt f (f x)
Function.IsFixedPt.apply.description: If a point is a fixed point of a function, then applying the function to that point results in the same fixed point.

Function.IsFixedPt.preimage_iterate.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.preimage_iterate.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} {s : Set α} (h : IsFixedPt (Set.preimage f) s)
  (n : ℕ) : IsFixedPt (Set.preimage f^[n]) s

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.preimage: The preimage of a set under a function consists of all elements that map into the set when the function is applied.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Function.IsFixedPt.preimage_iterate.description: If a set is a fixed point of the preimage of a function, it remains a fixed point of the preimage of that function applied repeatedly any number of times.

Function.IsFixedPt.equiv_symm.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.equiv_symm.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {e : Perm α} (h : IsFixedPt (⇑e) x) :
  IsFixedPt (⇑(Equiv.symm e)) x

explanatories.Equiv.Perm: This definition introduces the type that represents all bijections from a set to itself.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

Function.IsFixedPt.equiv_symm.description: If a point is a fixed point of a permutation, it is also a fixed point of the inverse permutation.

Function.IsFixedPt.perm_inv.code: Function.IsFixedPt.perm_inv.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {e : Perm α} (h : IsFixedPt (⇑e) x) : IsFixedPt (⇑e⁻¹) x

explanatories.Equiv.Perm: This definition introduces the type that represents all bijections from a set to itself.

Function.IsFixedPt.perm_inv.description: If a point is a fixed point of a permutation, then it is also a fixed point of its inverse permutation.

Function.IsFixedPt.perm_pow.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.perm_pow.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {e : Perm α} (h : IsFixedPt (⇑e) x) (n : ℕ) :
  IsFixedPt (⇑(e ^ n)) x

explanatories.Equiv.Perm: This definition introduces the type that represents all bijections from a set to itself.

Function.IsFixedPt.perm_pow.description: If a point is a fixed point of a permutation, then it remains a fixed point when the permutation is raised to any natural number power.

Function.IsFixedPt.perm_zpow.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.perm_zpow.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {e : Perm α} (h : IsFixedPt (⇑e) x) (n : ℤ) :
  IsFixedPt (⇑(e ^ n)) x

explanatories.Equiv.Perm: This definition introduces the type that represents all bijections from a set to itself.

Function.IsFixedPt.perm_zpow.description: If a point is a fixed point of a permutation, it remains a fixed point when that permutation is raised to any integer power.

Function.Injective.isFixedPt_apply_iff.code:
Function.Injective.isFixedPt_apply_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} (hf : Injective f) {x : α} :
  IsFixedPt f (f x) ↔ IsFixedPt f x

explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.

Function.Injective.isFixedPt_apply_iff.description: A point is a fixed point of a function applied to itself if and only if it is a fixed point of the function.

Function.fixedPoints.code: Function.fixedPoints.{u} {α : Type u} (f : α → α) : Set α
Function.fixedPoints.comment: The set of fixed points of a map `f : α → α`.

explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Function.fixedPoints.fullDefinition: def fixedPoints (f : α → α) : Set α :=   { x : α | IsFixedPt f x }
Function.fixedPoints.description: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.

Function.IsFixedPt.decidable.code: Function.IsFixedPt.decidable.{u} {α : Type u} [h : DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {x : α} : Decidable (IsFixedPt f x)

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Function.IsFixedPt.decidable.fullDefinition: instance decidable [h : DecidableEq α] {f : α → α} {x : α} : Decidable (IsFixedPt f x) :=   h (f x) x
Function.IsFixedPt.decidable.description: It is possible to decide whether a given point is a fixed point of a function when the type of the input has a decidable equality.

Function.fixedPoints.decidable.code: Function.fixedPoints.decidable.{u} {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] (f : α → α) (x : α) : Decidable (x ∈ fixedPoints f)

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt.decidable: It is possible to decide whether a given point is a fixed point of a function when the type of the input has a decidable equality.

Function.fixedPoints.decidable.fullDefinition: instance fixedPoints.decidable [DecidableEq α] (f : α → α) (x : α) :     Decidable (x ∈ fixedPoints f) :=   IsFixedPt.decidable
Function.fixedPoints.decidable.description: It is possible to determine whether a specific point is a fixed point of a function within a decidable equality context.

Function.mem_fixedPoints.code: Function.mem_fixedPoints.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} {x : α} : x ∈ fixedPoints f ↔ IsFixedPt f x

explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.
explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.

Function.mem_fixedPoints.description: A point is in the set of fixed points of a function if and only if it is a fixed point of that function.

Function.mem_fixedPoints_iff.code: Function.mem_fixedPoints_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f : α → α} {x : α} : x ∈ fixedPoints f ↔ f x = x

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.

Function.mem_fixedPoints_iff.description: A point is in the set of fixed points of a function if and only if it is equal to its image under that function.

Function.fixedPoints_id.code: Function.fixedPoints_id.{u} {α : Type u} : fixedPoints id = Set.univ
Function.fixedPoints_id.description: The set of fixed points of the identity function is the entire space.

Function.fixedPoints_subset_range.code: Function.fixedPoints_subset_range.{u} {α : Type u} {f : α → α} : fixedPoints f ⊆ Set.range f

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Function.fixedPoints_subset_range.description: The set of fixed points of a function is a subset of the range of that function.

Function.Semiconj.mapsTo_fixedPoints.code:
Function.Semiconj.mapsTo_fixedPoints.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {fa : α → α} {fb : β → β} {g : α → β}
  (h : Semiconj g fa fb) : Set.MapsTo g (fixedPoints fa) (fixedPoints fb)
Function.Semiconj.mapsTo_fixedPoints.comment:
If `g` semiconjugates `fa` to `fb`, then it sends fixed points of `fa` to fixed points
of `fb`.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.MapsTo: A function maps to a set if the image of that set is contained within another specified set.

Function.Semiconj.mapsTo_fixedPoints.description: If one function semiconjugates another, then it maps the fixed points of the first function to the fixed points of the second function.

Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.code:
Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (g : β → α) :
  Set.InvOn f g (fixedPoints (f ∘ g)) (fixedPoints (g ∘ f))
Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.comment:
Any two maps `f : α → β` and `g : β → α` are inverse of each other on the sets of fixed points
of `f ∘ g` and `g ∘ f`, respectively.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.InvOn: An inverse of a function with respect to two sets signifies that one function can retrieve the original input for every element in the second set based on the output from the first function.

Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.description: Two functions are seen as inverses of each other when restricted to their respective sets of fixed points derived from their compositions.

Function.mapsTo_fixedPoints_comp.code:
Function.mapsTo_fixedPoints_comp.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (g : β → α) :
  Set.MapsTo f (fixedPoints (g ∘ f)) (fixedPoints (f ∘ g))
Function.mapsTo_fixedPoints_comp.comment: Any map `f` sends fixed points of `g ∘ f` to fixed points of `f ∘ g`.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.MapsTo: A function maps to a set if the image of that set is contained within another specified set.

Function.mapsTo_fixedPoints_comp.description: A function sends the fixed points of the composition of two functions in one order to the fixed points of their composition in the reverse order.

Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp.code:
Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (g : β → α) :
  Set.BijOn g (fixedPoints (f ∘ g)) (fixedPoints (g ∘ f))
Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp.comment:
Given two maps `f : α → β` and `g : β → α`, `g` is a bijective map between the fixed points
of `f ∘ g` and the fixed points of `g ∘ f`. The inverse map is `f`, see `invOn_fixedPoints_comp`.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.BijOn: A function is bijective from one set to another if it is both injective on the first set and its image under the function is exactly the second set.

Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp.description: A function acting on fixed points of a composition of two maps establishes a bijective correspondence between the fixed points of each composition.

Function.Commute.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.code:
Function.Commute.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : α → α} (h : Function.Commute f g) :
  Set.InvOn f g (fixedPoints (f ∘ g)) (fixedPoints (f ∘ g))
Function.Commute.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.comment:
If self-maps `f` and `g` commute, then they are inverse of each other on the set of fixed points
of `f ∘ g`. This is a particular case of `Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp`.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.InvOn: An inverse of a function with respect to two sets signifies that one function can retrieve the original input for every element in the second set based on the output from the first function.
explanatories.Function.invOn_fixedPoints_comp: Two functions are seen as inverses of each other when restricted to their respective sets of fixed points derived from their compositions.

Function.Commute.invOn_fixedPoints_comp.description: If two functions commute, they act as inverses on the set of fixed points of their composition.

Function.Commute.left_bijOn_fixedPoints_.code:
Function.Commute.left_bijOn_fixedPoints_comp.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : α → α} (h : Function.Commute f g) :
  Set.BijOn f (fixedPoints (f ∘ g)) (fixedPoints (f ∘ g))
Function.Commute.left_bijOn_fixedPoints_.comment:
If self-maps `f` and `g` commute, then `f` is bijective on the set of fixed points of `f ∘ g`.
This is a particular case of `Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp`.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.BijOn: A function is bijective from one set to another if it is both injective on the first set and its image under the function is exactly the second set.

Function.Commute.left_bijOn_fixedPoints_.description: If two functions commute, then one function is bijective on the set of fixed points of their composition.

Function.Commute.right_bijOn_fixedPoints.code:
Function.Commute.right_bijOn_fixedPoints_comp.{u} {α : Type u} {f g : α → α} (h : Function.Commute f g) :
  Set.BijOn g (fixedPoints (f ∘ g)) (fixedPoints (f ∘ g))
Function.Commute.right_bijOn_fixedPoints.comment:
If self-maps `f` and `g` commute, then `g` is bijective on the set of fixed points of `f ∘ g`.
This is a particular case of `Function.bijOn_fixedPoints_comp`.

explanatories.Function.fixedPoints: The set of fixed points of a function consists of all points that remain unchanged when the function is applied to them.
explanatories.Set.BijOn: A function is bijective from one set to another if it is both injective on the first set and its image under the function is exactly the second set.

Function.Commute.right_bijOn_fixedPoints.description: If two functions commute, then the second function is bijective on the set of fixed points of their composition.

isFixedPt_of_tendsto_iterate.code:
isFixedPt_of_tendsto_iterate.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace α] [T2Space α] {f : α → α} {x y : α}

If the iterates `f^[n] x` converge to `y` and `f` is continuous at `y`,
then `y` is a fixed point for `f`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.
explanatories.ContinuousAt: This defines the condition for a function between topological spaces to be continuous at a specific point by ensuring that the function values approach the value at that point as the input approaches it.
explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.

isFixedPt_of_tendsto_iterate.description: If a sequence formed by repeatedly applying a function converges to a point and that function is continuous at that point, then the point is a fixed point of the function.

is_closed_fixed_points.code:
isClosed_fixedPoints.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace α] [T2Space α] {f : α → α} (hf : Continuous f) :

Function.IsPeriodicPt.code: Function.IsPeriodicPt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (f : α → α) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : Prop
Function.IsPeriodicPt.comment:
A point `x` is a periodic point of `f : α → α` of period `n` if `f^[n] x = x`.
Note that we do not require `0 < n` in this definition. Many theorems about periodic points
need this assumption.

explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.

Function.IsPeriodicPt.fullDefinition: def IsPeriodicPt (f : α → α) (n : ℕ) (x : α) :=   IsFixedPt f^[n] x
Function.IsPeriodicPt.description: A point is considered periodic with respect to a function if applying that function repeatedly a certain number of times returns the point to its original position.

Function.IsFixedPt.isPeriodicPt.code:
Function.IsFixedPt.isPeriodicPt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f : α → α} {x : α} (hf : IsFixedPt f x) (n : ℕ) :
  IsPeriodicPt f n x
Function.IsFixedPt.isPeriodicPt.comment: A fixed point of `f` is a periodic point of `f` of any prescribed period.

explanatories.Function.IsPeriodicPt: A point is considered periodic with respect to a function if applying that function repeatedly a certain number of times returns the point to its original position.

Function.IsFixedPt.isPeriodicPt.description: A point that remains unchanged when a function is applied is also considered to return to its original position after any number of applications of that function.

Function.is_periodic_id.code: Function.is_periodic_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (n : ℕ) (x : α) : IsPeriodicPt id n x
Function.is_periodic_id.comment: For the identity map, all points are periodic.

explanatories.Function.IsPeriodicPt: A point is considered periodic with respect to a function if applying that function repeatedly a certain number of times returns the point to its original position.

Function.is_periodic_id.description: Every point is considered periodic for the identity function, regardless of the period chosen.

Function.isPeriodicPt_zero.code: Function.isPeriodicPt_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (f : α → α) (x : α) : IsPeriodicPt f 0 x
Function.isPeriodicPt_zero.comment: Any point is a periodic point of period `0`.

explanatories.Function.IsPeriodicPt: A point is considered periodic with respect to a function if applying that function repeatedly a certain number of times returns the point to its original position.

Function.isPeriodicPt_zero.description: Every point is considered a periodic point with period zero for any function.

Function.IsPeriodicPt.isFixedPt.code:

explanatories.Function.IsFixedPt: A fixed point of a function is defined as a point that remains unchanged when the function is applied to it.

Function.IsPeriodicPt.isFixedPt.description: If a point is periodic with respect to a function at a certain period, then that point is also a fixed point when the function is applied that many times.

Function.IsPeriodicPt.map.code:

Function.IsPeriodicPt.map.description: If a point is periodic with respect to one function, it remains periodic with the same period when mapped through a semiconjugate function.

Function.IsPeriodicPt.apply_iterate.code:
Function.IsPeriodicPt.apply_iterate.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f : α → α} {x : α} {n : ℕ} (hx : IsPeriodicPt f n x) (m : ℕ) :

Function.IsPeriodicPt.eq_1.description: A point is periodic with respect to a function if and only if that point remains unchanged after the function is applied a corresponding number of times.

Function.IsPeriodicPt.add.code:

The orbit of a periodic point `x` of `f` is the cycle `[x, f x, f (f x), ...]`. Its length is

birkhoffSum.code: birkhoffSum.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : M
birkhoffSum.comment: The sum of values of `g` on the first `n` points of the orbit of `x` under `f`.

explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.

birkhoffSum.fullDefinition: def birkhoffSum (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : M := ∑ k ∈ range n, g (f^[k] x)
birkhoffSum.description: This defines a function that computes the sum of values produced by another function over the first `n` points in the sequence generated by iteratively applying a transformation to a starting point.

birkhoffSum_zero.code:
birkhoffSum_zero.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (x : α) :
  birkhoffSum f g 0 x = 0
birkhoffSum_zero.description: This theorem states that the sum computed by the defined function is zero when considering zero terms from the sequence generated by the transformation.

birkhoffSum_one.code:
birkhoffSum_one.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (x : α) :
  birkhoffSum f g 1 x = g x
birkhoffSum_one.description: This theorem states that the sum obtained from considering one term in the sequence is equal to the value of the function at the starting point.

birkhoffSum_succ.code:
birkhoffSum_succ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) :
  birkhoffSum f g (n + 1) x = birkhoffSum f g n x + g (f^[n] x)
birkhoffSum_succ.description: This theorem expresses that the sum calculated for one more term in the sequence can be derived by adding the value of the function at the latest point in the orbit to the sum of the previous terms.

birkhoffSum_succ'.code:
birkhoffSum_succ'.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) :
  birkhoffSum f g (n + 1) x = g x + birkhoffSum f g n (f x)
birkhoffSum_succ'.description: This theorem states that the sum computed for one more term in the sequence is equal to the value of the function at the initial point plus the sum of the previous terms evaluated at the transformed point.

birkhoffAverage.code:
birkhoffAverage.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) {α : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [DivisionSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
  [Module R M] (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : M
birkhoffAverage.comment:
The average value of `g` on the first `n` points of the orbit of `x` under `f`,
i.e. the Birkhoff sum `∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, g (f^[k] x)` divided by `n`.

This average appears in many ergodic theorems
which say that `(birkhoffAverage R f g · x)`
converges to the "space average" `⨍ x, g x ∂μ` as `n → ∞`.

We use an auxiliary `[DivisionSemiring R]` to define division by `n`.
However, the definition does not depend on the choice of `R`,
see `birkhoffAverage_congr_ring`.

explanatories.birkhoffSum: This defines a function that computes the sum of values produced by another function over the first `n` points in the sequence generated by iteratively applying a transformation to a starting point.

birkhoffAverage.fullDefinition: def birkhoffAverage (f : α → α) (g : α → M) (n : ℕ) (x : α) : M := (n : R)⁻¹ • birkhoffSum f g n x

map_birkhoffAverage.code:

dist_birkhoffSum_apply_birkhoffSum.description: The theorem shows that the distance between the summed values of a function applied to an iterated point and the original point is equal to the distance between the images of these points under another function.

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.

dist_birkhoffAverage_apply_birkhoffAvera.description: The theorem establishes that the distance between the averaged values of a function applied to an iterated point and the original point is equal to the distance between the images of these points under another function, scaled by the reciprocal of the number of points averaged.

tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkho.code:
tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  (𝕜 : Type u_3) [RCLike 𝕜] [Module 𝕜 E] [BoundedSMul 𝕜 E] {f : α → α} {g : α → E} {x : α}
  (h : Bornology.IsBounded (range fun x_1 => g (f^[x_1] x))) :
  Tendsto (fun n => birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n (f x) - birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n x) atTop (𝓝 0)
tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkho.comment:
If a function `g` is bounded along the positive orbit of `x` under `f`,
then the difference between Birkhoff averages of `g`
along the orbit of `f x` and along the orbit of `x`
tends to zero.

See also `tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkhoffAverage'`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.
explanatories.Bornology.IsBounded: This introduces a predicate that determines whether a given set is bounded with respect to the specified bornology.

tendsto_birkhoffAverage_apply_sub_birkho.description: The theorem states that if a function is bounded along the positive iterations of a point, then the difference between the Birkhoff averages computed along those iterations converges to zero as the number of iterations increases.

dist_birkhoffAverage_birkhoffAverage_le.code:
dist_birkhoffAverage_birkhoffAverage_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  (𝕜 : Type u_3) [RCLike 𝕜] [Module 𝕜 E] [BoundedSMul 𝕜 E] (f : α → α) (g : α → E) (n : ℕ) (x y : α) :
  dist (birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n x) (birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f g n y) ≤
    (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, dist (g (f^[k] x)) (g (f^[k] y))) / ↑n

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

dist_birkhoffAverage_birkhoffAverage_le.description: The theorem establishes that the distance between the Birkhoff averages computed from two different starting points is bounded by the average of the distances of their corresponding image values under another function over a finite number of iterations.

uniformEquicontinuous_birkhoffAverage.comment:
If `f` is a non-strictly contracting map (i.e., it is Lipschitz with constant `1`)
and `g` is a uniformly continuous, then the Birkhoff averages of `g` along orbits of `f`
is a uniformly equicontinuous family of functions.

explanatories.LipschitzWith: A function is Lipschitz continuous with a non-negative constant if the distance between its outputs is bounded by the constant multiplied by the distance between its inputs.
explanatories.UniformContinuous: A function is uniformly continuous if the images of close points remain close, regardless of their locations in the original space.
explanatories.UniformEquicontinuous: A family of functions between uniform spaces is considered uniformly equicontinuous if, for every entourage, there exists another entourage such that when points are close in the second space, their images under the functions remain close in the first space.

uniformEquicontinuous_birkhoffAverage.description: The theorem states that if a function is Lipschitz continuous with a constant of one and another function is uniformly continuous, then the Birkhoff averages of the second function along the orbits of the first function form a uniformly equicontinuous family of functions.

Polynomial.newtonMap.comment:
Given a single-variable polynomial `P` with derivative `P'`, this is the map:
`x ↦ x - P(x) / P'(x)`. When `P'(x)` is not a unit we use a junk-value pattern and send `x ↦ x`.

explanatories.Ring.inverse: This defines a function that maps each element of a monoid with zero to its inverse if it is invertible, and to zero if it is not.

Polynomial.newtonMap.description: This definition describes a function that applies a specific iterative method for finding roots of a polynomial, adjusting the input based on the polynomial value and its derivative.

explanatories.continuous_fst: This theorem asserts that the first projection function from a product space to one of its component spaces is continuous.
explanatories.continuous_subtype_val: This theorem states that the value function of a subtype in a topological space is continuous.

explanatories.Continuous.subtype_mk: This theorem establishes that if a function is continuous and maps into a subset defined by a property, then the function extended to create a subtype from its output remains continuous.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.Flow.toFun: This defines a function that represents the action of a flow from one topological space to another.
explanatories.Flow.cont': The flow defined between two topological spaces is continuous when viewed as a function that takes a pair of inputs from the flow's domain and acts on the range.

  (f : Filter τ) (ϕ : τ → α → β) (s : Set α) (y : β) :
  y ∈ ω f ϕ s ↔ ∀ n ∈ 𝓝 y, ∃ᶠ (t : τ) in f, (s ∩ ϕ t ⁻¹' n).Nonempty
mem_omegaLimit_iff_frequently.comment:
An element `y` is in the ω-limit set of `s` w.r.t. `f` if the
preimages of an arbitrary neighbourhood of `y` frequently
(w.r.t. `f`) intersects of `s`.

CircleDeg1Lift.semiconj_of_group_action_.code:
CircleDeg1Lift.semiconj_of_group_action_of_forall_translationNumber_eq.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G]
  (f₁ f₂ : G →* CircleDeg1Lift) (h : ∀ (g : G), τ (f₁ g) = τ (f₂ g)) : ∃ F, ∀ (g : G), Semiconj ⇑F ⇑(f₁ g) ⇑(f₂ g)
CircleDeg1Lift.semiconj_of_group_action_.comment:
Consider two actions `f₁ f₂ : G →* CircleDeg1Lift` of a group on the real line by lifts of
orientation preserving circle homeomorphisms. Suppose that for each `g : G` the homeomorphisms
`f₁ g` and `f₂ g` have equal rotation numbers. Then there exists `F : CircleDeg1Lift` such that
`F * f₁ g = f₂ g * F` for all `g : G`.

This is a version of Proposition 5.4 from [Étienne Ghys, Groupes d'homeomorphismes du cercle et
cohomologie bornee][ghys87:groupes].

explanatories.Function.Semiconj: A function is said to semiconjugate two mappings if applying the function before one mapping is the same as applying the other mapping after the function.

CircleDeg1Lift.semiconj_of_group_action_.description: This theorem indicates that if two group actions on a CircleDeg1Lift have the same translation number for every group element, there exists a specific element in the CircleDeg1Lift that semiconjugates the two actions.

A self-map preserving a finite measure is conservative: if `μ s ≠ 0`, then at least one point
`x ∈ s` comes back to `s` under iterations of `f`. Actually, a.e. point of `s` comes back to `s`
infinitely many times, see `MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.conservative` and theorems about
`MeasureTheory.Conservative`.

with a countable family of measurable sets separating the points of `X`.
